content: The coadministration of phosphodiesterase inhibitors with clarithromycin, a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, is not recommended due to the potential for increased systemic exposure to these drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider reducing the dosage of the phosphodiesterase inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Additionally, both clarithromycin and siponimod prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution or alternative therapy. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and solifenacin prolong the QTc interval, so avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as clarithromycin, should not be coadministered with sonidegib. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming therapy. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by mechanisms involving active secretion via OATP1. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as inhibition of OATP1 may increase sulbactam plasma concentrations. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and sunitinib prolong the QTc interval, so avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and tacrolimus prolong the QTc interval, so avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day, or for as-needed use, limit to 10 mg every 72 hours. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If P-gp inhibitors are discontinued, increase the talazoparib dose after 3–5 half-lives of the inhibitor. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with tazemetostat. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Thioridazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tipranavir and clarithromycin mutually increase each other’s levels by reducing metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. No dose adjustment is necessary in normal renal function, but reduce the clarithromycin dose by 50% if creatinine clearance is 30–60 mL/min. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. Clarithromycin increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of toremifene with QT-prolonging agents should be avoided. If concomitant use is required, interrupt toremifene therapy or closely monitor the patient. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day prior to the next infusion. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both trazodone and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval, so avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and triclabendazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Trifluoperazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Trimipramine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the live bacterial vaccine. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. Clarithromycin and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vandetanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin and vardenafil both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Vemurafenib and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and vorinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of zavegepant intranasal by mechanisms involving OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant. Clarithromycin and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the dose used prior to initiating the inhibitor. Albuterol and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and alfuzosin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of apalutamide with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. Arformoterol and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Azithromycin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive substrate in accordance with its prescribing information. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely.
